newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas down on aggressive trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas down on aggressive trade.

text.p: Gasoline edged down on Tuesday amid aggressive offers and weaker crude, traders said.
A Dutch trader offered 95-octane unleaded gasoline at $24.05 per barrel but later sold the cargo to a Japanese trader at a much lower level of $23.75 for 50,000-barrel lifting June 11-15.
On Monday, a U.S. major sold 100,000-barrels of the same grade lifting June 10-12 to a Japanese trader at $24.10.
Some sellers were skeptical about the low deal level.
"Mogas depends on the supply and demand siutation, not an individual deal. I would rather look at the IOC number," said a seller.
Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) tender for 25,000-tonnes of 87-octane 0.15 g/l lead gasoline for June 10-14 delivery to Bombay, closes on May 28 and is valid for a day.
Singapore reforming margins were under further pressure with feedstock naphtha prices holding steady amid lack of firm direction.
Naphtha swaps were largely unchanged with June quoted at $22.50/$22.60 per barrel and July at $22.55/$22.70.
But firm outright prices were putting a dampener on Singapore fob premiums which were assessed at a low 40 cents per barrel.
